runs.answer:
Sure! Here's a simple way to explain it:

Inflation is when things slowly start to cost more money over time.

Imagine a candy bar costs $1 today. If inflation happens, next year that same candy bar might cost $1.05. Your dollar buys a little less candy than it did before. So the money in your piggy bank can buy less than it could last year.

Why does it happen? Sometimes lots of people want to buy things, but there aren't quite enough to go around. Stores can charge more because people are still willing to pay. Also, when it costs more to make things, like sugar or the trucks that bring candy to the store, the stores often raise their prices to cover that.

Most of the time, prices go up just a little bit each year. That's normal and expected.
